# connection:press-fit-bearing-15x10x3

**15x10x3 bearing seated by interference — Ø10 inner ring on a printed boss, Ø15 outer ring in a printed pocket**

- **a** — the 15x10x3 ball bearing (part:bearing-15x10x3), interface 'bore' (Ø10.0, inner ring) or 'od' (Ø15.0, outer ring) — dimensions measured off Pollen's own mesh, no vendor designation exists in the reference
- **b** — the seat: a Ø10 boss for the inner ring (interface 'shaft'/'boss' — microduck-shin 'ankle', Ø10.0 x 3.2) or a Ø15 pocket for the outer ring ('housing_bore'/'pocket' — microduck-ankle 'ankle_bearing', Ø15.0 x 2.3 with Ø16 x 0.5 lead-in); the microduck shelf's role 'bearing_seat' with either name also serves

## Verdict: PASS

The GEOMETRY of the joint is PASS and it is measured on both sides: the ring is Ø10.0 bore / Ø15.0 OD / 3.0 wide (cecad.meshfeatures + bbox on seeed_bearing__configuration_default.stl, 2026-09-02, frozen in evidence/bearing-15x10x3-geometry.json), and the reference design's own seats measure at the same nominals — shin 'ankle' boss Ø10.0 x 3.2 for the inner ring, ankle 'ankle_bearing' pocket Ø15.0 x 2.3 for the outer (each quoted in that part's own interfaces.json, measured off Pollen's meshes). What stays CANNOT DETERMINE is stated per-check in compat.py and as ledger rows, not rounded away: the INTERFERENCE — the seats are FDM-printed PLA with no ISO class and the unnamed ring has no vendor tolerance sheet, so grip and press force are unmeasurable until calipers meet the actual ring (ring_deviation_um) and the as-printed bore (measured_d_mm); and the PARTIAL ENGAGEMENT — Pollen's own ankle pocket is 2.3 mm deep for the 3 mm ring (deliberate: the proud 0.7 mm clears the shin boss), and whether 77% engagement holds the press is a bench question. compat.py grades what can be graded and refuses the rest by name.

## Standard

**ISO 286-1 (limits and fits — the k6/h6/H7 grading compat.py can do WHEN a class is declared) / ISO 286-2 (the published tables; two IT7 values transcribed, see why)** — ISO 286 defines the only fit language compat.py grades in, and its limits are DERIVED from ISO 286-1's own formulae (i = 0.45*cbrt(D) + 0.001*D; IT6 = 10i; k: ei = +0.6*cbrt(D)) — reproducing the published 10 k6 (+1/+10), 10 h6 (-9/0) and 15 k6 (+1/+12) exactly. MEASURED 2026-09-02 by this folder's own self-test: the published tables are NOT pure formula output — IT7 in the 6-10 and 10-18 steps is published as 15 and 18 um where raw 16i gives 14.37 and 17.32 — so those two values are TRANSCRIBED from ISO 286-2 with the drift recorded in compat.py (PUBLISHED_IT7_UM) and in the ledger, not hidden inside a 'derivation'. The standard governs the GRADING VOCABULARY only: the reference design's actual seats are FDM PLA and carry no class, which is why the folder's fit verdict on those pairs is per-measurement, not per-class.

## What it adds to the BOM

`part:bearing-15x10x3`

An interference fit adds no fastener; it adds the bearing itself, because a connection that seats a bearing is the reason the bearing appears in the BOM (the press-fit-608 rule). part:bearing-15x10x3 resolves on this shelf (checked 2026-09-02). No circlip is ever added: no circlip groove exists on any measured microduck seat and no circlip folder is on this shelf — mate() refuses the option by name rather than dangling a ref.

## The joint

- holds by **form**, removable: True, transmits axial, shear
- rating: ring_d_mm = 10.0, ring_D_mm = 15.0, ring_B_mm = 3.0, grip_N = **MISSING**, reference_speed_rpm = **MISSING**

TWO holds_by values live in this folder, the press-fit-608 split kept verbatim: the SEAT is held by FRICTION (the interference) and leaves nothing free; the ROTATION is held by FORM, by the rolling elements, and lives ACROSS the two seats. This block describes the spanning case, which is what dof_left describes, so holds_by is form; mate() on a single seat returns all locked with holds_by 'friction' and says so. driven false: the ankle is driven by its XL330 through the horn joint on the other side of the shin — this bearing is the idler side. rating: ring dimensions MEASURED (meshfeatures); grip_N and reference_speed_rpm MISSING — no vendor sheet exists for this unnamed ring and no bench has touched one here.
